owner: Combat (CombatSnapshot, CombatAttempt, CombatResolution, report blob, isolated resolver). Character/stat owners, I5, Generation and every mode keep their existing ownership.
rules: A mode starts combat only inside its own caller transaction (RepeatableRead or Serializable) by calling Combat START with an authenticated actor, domain kind, authority scope/generation, source-shaped domain locator, start fingerprint, trust profile SERVER_REPORT_AUTHORITATIVE_V1, participants and result deadline. Combat never queries mode tables or owns mode ranks, rewards, cooldowns or calendars.

Participants are OWNED_SELF, OWNED_FOREIGN or TEMPLATE. Owned actors are frozen from the publicstats 3B validated observation gather in the same CA8 CoherentReadScope: no second owner read path, no foreign SQL, no locks taken by readers. TEMPLATE actors carry fully specified source params from a mode-versioned mapping validated against the pinned content and fighter-class manifest. BORROWED and CLIENT_ATTESTED are not implemented by this contract.

The snapshot is immutable, canonically serialized and SHA-256 addressed. It records snapshot schema, content revision, rules corpus id, source archive identity, trust/entropy/adapter policy versions, decision instant, owner state versions and, per actor, origin, identity and source-shaped params plus the 3B battle-total facet; per player it records the collection attr and exclusive book count. Later owner mutation never changes a frozen attempt.

Any missing, unavailable, stale or unqualified provider refuses START with a typed error; legitimate absence is explicit. Any actor or statically known summon target whose class is absent from the corpus fighter-class manifest refuses START with CLASS_UNAVAILABLE_IN_PINNED_PROFILE. No fallback class, default zero or substituted outcome exists.

One unresolved attempt per (domain kind, authority scope, locator). Equivalent START (same fingerprint) returns the same attempt, snapshot, entropy and, when present, report; a different fingerprint while unresolved is a typed conflict. START commits before any resolver work. Combat attempt lock rank is 609 (after mode roots 601..608, before I5 Grant 610+).

Entropy follows inherited 418 HMAC_SHA256_COUNTER_LUA_RANDOM_COMPAT_V1: root = HMAC-SHA256(key[version], 'gxb-combat/v1' || attempt_id || snapshot_hash || policy_version) from a configured secret key ring; missing key version fails closed; retired keys stay available for historical reconstruction. os.time is the frozen decision instant; math.randomseed rekeys the attempt-local stream.

Resolution runs after START commit, outside DB locks, in a separate worker process per attempt with only the bounded snapshot and the embedded rules corpus: no DB credentials, network, filesystem corpus lookup, wall clock or owner ports. OS wall deadline kill, memory/CPU/file rlimits and bounded stdin/stdout/stderr apply. Crash, timeout or resource kill leaves the attempt retryable with identical inputs; deterministic script or validation failure is permanent. Output is revalidated in Go before persistence.

Snapshot-only adapters (SNAPSHOT_ONLY_ADAPTERS_V1): leading-BOM strip, isClient=false after const.lua, lib.battle.app.model.Item -> app.model.Item, lib.spirit.spirit_item throwing guard, lib.player.backpack answering only frozen exclusive book items, per-owner selfPlayer {playerID, albumAttr}, recovered list.reduce and Game/Misc design viewport, render/scheduler/JSON shims and a transport-detached report driver. Sparse table MaxArrayIndex 65536 is a profile setting requiring qualification.

C5A_COMBAT_COLLECTION_ATTR_OWNER_SCOPED_V1 (private reconstruction policy): each participant's own collection attr applies to that participant's actors and is emitted as hero_collect_attr[player]; zhuge_book_skill_num[player] is emitted from the frozen count. This does not change the 3B public-view rule.

Resolution persists once: immutable CombatResolution plus report blob (hash, encoding, length, rules version). Duplicate worker completion with identical hash is idempotent; a differing hash is an integrity failure. Replay loads materialized data and never reruns entropy. Durable outcome is separate from replay retention, which is mode-owned.

Terminal settlement happens once in the mode's caller transaction: Combat TERMINAL transition validates attempt/state version/generation and returns the immutable resolution; the mode applies its own transition and I5 Grant/Mail/Objective ports and a semantic receipt in the same transaction. Unknown COMMIT is resolved by positive receipt/postcondition evidence only; absence is ResolutionUnknown and never authorizes a blind retry.

Internal attempt UUID never becomes a stock-wire requirement. The rules corpus is a generated, hash-manifested product artifact compiled from source archive c7e98789...; START requires the active content manifest source_archive_sha256 to equal the corpus source archive.
This foundation qualifies no mode, ranking, history, cosmetic origin or full I7C4 gate. Mode leaves 5B..5F remain separately researched, authorized and qualified.
